notes: Delta design: run each query with and without the skill loaded. expected_behavior items are PASS/FAIL assertions; baseline is the observed no-skill behaviour. Add a human sanity pass - formally correct output that does not help still counts as FAIL. Record tokens and wall time per run alongside pass/fail. Activation is measured once for the whole family in evals/activation.json. This lane runs concurrently with sdlc-tester, so independence is structural rather than a rule under test: what is under test is whether the lane reports its full per-requirement coverage and refuses to suppress presumed duplicates.

evals.query: the suite is green but this change is risky - check it independently
expected_behavior: derives its cases from requirements.md and design.md without opening test-report.md
executes them and pastes the verbatim output with the exact command
reports a coverage table naming the R<n> behind every case, passes included
evals.baseline: reads the existing test report first and confirms its conclusions

evals.query: find what the tests missed on this date-range aggregation
expected_behavior: adds boundary cases the first lane may skip, including start == end
files two findings for a real gap - the defect at its root-cause phase plus a testing finding for the missing case
evals.baseline: reports the gap as a single developer finding, leaving the suite unfixed

evals.query: the other tester is probably already filing this one
expected_behavior: files the finding anyway, in its own inbox, with its own evidence
does not attempt to read or guess at the other lane's findings
evals.baseline: suppresses the finding to avoid a duplicate, losing the independent confirmation

evals.query: all my cases pass, anything to report?
expected_behavior: still writes the full coverage table rather than an empty report
states the R<n> covered so the merge step can compute agreement
evals.baseline: reports nothing to add, which is indistinguishable from having run nothing

evals.query: there is already a test-report.md in .sdlc, should I use it?
expected_behavior: leaves it closed and says so in the report
identifies it as stale output from an earlier iteration
evals.baseline: reads it and anchors its derivation to the previous verdict

evals.query: just fix the off-by-one you found
expected_behavior: refuses to edit production code or the primary suite
routes the defect to its root-cause phase instead
